title: The exponent-range conjecture for the four classical means
statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be positive real numbers, and let

$$
H=\frac{2xy}{x+y},\qquad G=\sqrt{xy},\qquad A=\frac{x+y}{2},\qquad Q=\sqrt{\frac{x^2+y^2}{2}}.
$$

For a real number $n$, consider the inequality

$$
A^n+G^n\le Q^n+H^n.
$$

**Exponent-range conjecture for the four classical means.** The inequality holds for every negative real number $n$ and every real number $n\geq\frac12$. Moreover, for every real number $n\in(0,\frac12)$, neither this inequality nor its converse holds universally for all positive real numbers $x$ and $y$. The conjecture asks for the complete real-exponent range of validity of the inequality; the source provides computational and graphical evidence but no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00542

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).
source_name: Romeo Meštrović and Miomir Andjić, “Two curious inequalities involving different means of two arguments”, arXiv:1804.00542 (2018).
